title: Fine-grained prefill credit scheduler and kernel adapter for interleaved decode handoff
author: Maya Thompson
description: Context: Under bursty prefill patterns we observed decode stalls and high KV churn when many prefill fragments race to populate KV slots. This PR implements a token-credit based PrefillCreditScheduler plus a lightweight KernelAdapter that exposes fragment readiness and ownership to the decode queue so prefill and decode can interleave without mass KV evictions. Goals: reduce tail latency, preserve decode throughput, minimize KV thrash, and enable conservative rollout. High-level changes: new scheduler that assigns per-request token credits based on recent sequence-length distribution and active KV occupancy; a KernelAdapter shim that negotiates a handoff token between prefill and decode kernels and emits backpressure when KV pressure is detected; request-router backpressure hook and runtime flag to opt-in. Design notes: scheduler keeps a small sliding window of active fragments per GPU and enforces soft credits so a single large prefill can only consume a fraction of decode capacity; adapter supports both standard kernels and quantized kernels via a compatibility layer. Compatibility and rollout: feature gated behind runtime flag --prefill-crediting and off by default. Plan: 2-week canary against dedicated pools, metrics guardrails (99.9th latency, KV miss rate, decode throughput). Tests: unit tests for scheduler logic, integration tests for handoff correctness, end-to-end perf runs using benchmark-lab harness across 8 batch shapes. Related work: builds on previous prefill/handshake PRs but takes a different approach by using token credits instead of window coalescing. Follow-ups: add a dedicated dashboard (TODO). Checklist: - [x] design doc linked - [x] unit tests - [x] integration tests - [x] perf benchmarks - [x] docs update - [ ] monitoring dashboard (follow-up)
